content.text: Yes. In the installed `agents` 0.27.0, the scheduler runs your method as `handler(timing.payload, schedule)` (`node_modules/agents/dist/scheduler-DZ3xQfeK.js:228-229`). Here `schedule` is built from the stored job by `_jobToSchedule`. The Agent wires named callbacks through as `(payload, schedule) => method.call(this, payload, schedule)` (`src-DgCbZtIR.js:1916`). So a callback written as `async myTask(payload, schedule)` gets the payload you passed to `this.schedule()` as its first argument and the `Schedule` record (id, callback, type, timing and so on) as its second.
